content:
maya: quick note: onboarding folks keep hitting a weird issue in the JS sample app where DEBUG logs leak X-RW-REQID despite REDACT=1. Happens during retry edgecases. raising because it tripped a couple of customers.

chris: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro? is this node-only or showing up in python sampleapp as well?

maya: node-specific so far. repro: run sampleapp with DEBUG_LOG=true, REDWOOD_REDACT=true. send a request that triggers the retry (simulate 503 on the first attempt). observed log line: ```DEBUG: request-id=req_abc123 attempts=2 path=/v1/generate``` — req_abc123 should be masked.

ravi: likely init ordering. Our OpenTelemetry redaction hook registers during telemetry.init which in sampleapp is lazy-loaded after the express app mounts logger middleware. If logger attaches a format that stashes structured fields before the scrubber is installed, redaction is bypassed.

maya: hmm we intentionally kept telemetry init later to speed cold starts for the quickstart. but that seems to trade DX for safety.

chris: other angle: retry code clones headers and replays them to the downstream client. I remember a previous bug where cloning kept a raw header in a nonstandard key (x-rw-reqid-original) which isn't inspected by the redact hook. Could be a double-whammy: clone + init order.

maya: i grepped the retry middleware and found `headers['x-rw-reqid-raw'] = headers['x-rw-reqid']` in the clone path. redactHook only looks for 'x-rw-reqid' and 'x-request-id'.

ravi: ok simple fixes: 1) make telemetry.init sync and run before any logger/express registration in sampleapps; 2) normalize header names during retry clone (lowercase keys) and run redactHook on the cloned headers.

chris: for backward compatibility, we should also add a defensive scrub at the logger format level: before writing, run redact on any string field that matches the reqid regex. That'll catch weird keys. test matrix: node 18/20, ts/js variants.

telemetry-bot: STACKTRACE NOTE: Related docs: https://playbook.redwood.ai/telemetry/init-order and an open issue #324 in infra/sampleapp talking about header cloning.

maya: i pushed a small PR with both changes (sync init + header normalization) and a unit test that simulates a retry and asserts the logger output contains "[REDACTED]" for request-id. link: https://git.redwood/infra/sampleapp/pull/901

ravi: running CI now. also add a short note in quickstart that sampleapps require telemetry init to happen before any other instrumentation; call out the potential perf tradeoff for cold starts.

chris: agree. also file a follow-up to add telemetry init helper into SDK so users don't have to think about order. maybe `redwood.telemetry.bootstrap()` that idempotently installs scrubbers synchronously.

maya: CI passed. validated locally on node18 and node20. DEBUG logs no longer show raw reqid on retry flows. will open a small migration blurb in the SDK changelog.

ravi: nice. can we also add a short troubleshooting entry to the onboarding guide: "If you see raw request ids in logs: ensure telemetry bootstrap runs before your logger and patch retry middleware". keeps support tickets down.

chris: +1. thanks for catching and fixing. closing when the README blurb is live.

maya: added README note and migration snippet. closing. :white_check_mark:
